title: eMudhra intermediate CA compromise
summary: Private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities were compromised. Anyone holding them could issue a certificate for any website. A client is exposed while it still trusts the roots those intermediates chain to.
canarySource: The 12 test hosts are the advisory's own (emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/#check). Each serves a certificate chained to one compromised intermediate.

distrustedRoots.name: AAA Certificate Services (Comodo, via the Sectigo cross-sign)

fixes.curl:/usr/bin/curl:darwin: macOS's built-in curl reads /etc/ssl/cert.pem, which Apple has not updated yet. The advisory's fix (backs the file up first, asks for your Mac password): sudo cp /etc/ssl/cert.pem /etc/ssl/cert.pem.bak && awk '/^(###|===) /{skip=0} /^=== .*\/CN=(AAA Certificate Services|emSign ECC Root CA - G3)$/{skip=1} !skip' /etc/ssl/cert.pem.bak | sudo tee /etc/ssl/cert.pem > /dev/null
fixes.python:/usr/bin/python3:darwin: Apple's built-in Python reads /etc/ssl/cert.pem too. Apply the same fix as for macOS curl (see the curl line), or use a Python whose certifi is 2026.10.19 or newer.
fixes.curl:linux: Update your distribution's ca-certificates package (Debian 12: 20250419~deb12u2, Debian 13: 20250419+deb13u1). Until it ships, see the advisory's Linux workaround.
fixes.python:linux: Update your distribution's ca-certificates package; Python's default context reads the system store.
fixes.curl: Update the CA bundle this curl uses (Homebrew: brew upgrade ca-certificates, fixed in 2026-09-25_1 and later).
fixes.node: Node bundles its own roots; the fix is pending upstream (nodejs/node#66871). Until a fixed release: run Node with --use-openssl-ca and SSL_CERT_FILE pointing at an updated bundle (for example the cleaned /etc/ssl/cert.pem), or use a Node built on the system store (Homebrew's node).
fixes.python-certifi: Upgrade certifi in this environment to 2026.10.19 or newer: pip install -U certifi (uv: uv lock --upgrade-package certifi).
fixes.python: Upgrade the CA bundle this Python uses. python.org builds: pip install -U certifi (2026.10.19+) or run 'Install Certificates.command'.
fixes.macos-system: Install the latest macOS update (System Settings → General → Software Update). Apple blocks the compromised certificates through its updates; Safari and Apple's apps use this layer.

notCovered: Compiled programs carry the roots of the toolchain that built them: rebuild Go programs with Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10; update Electron apps to 44.9.1, 43.8.1 or 42.11.16; Rust: rustls-webpki 0.103.16, webpki-roots 1.0.10. Browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari block the intermediates through their own updates; check yours at the advisory's #check page.

binaries.fix: Update cloudflared to 2026.10.2 or later (Homebrew: brew upgrade cloudflared). It carries its own trust list, per Cloudflare's advisory.
Upgrade Go to 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, then rebuild and redeploy every program built with it: a Go program carries the roots of the Go that built it.
